evals.prompt: This is a conventional ASP.NET Core MVC app (Contoso.Web) with a normal wwwroot folder. We don't have any shared CDN — it's just this app's own CSS, JS, and favicon. Assets.Dockerfile derives from codebeltnet/web-cdn-origin:2.0.0 and copies a clean-checkout-reproducible wwwroot to /cdnroot. wwwroot stays as the conventional authoring root.

Keeps wwwroot as the authoring root and uses /cdnroot as the container content root

Adds a derived production image: FROM codebeltnet/web-cdn-origin:2.0.0 + COPY --chown=65532:65532 ./wwwroot/ /cdnroot/
Names the derived Dockerfile Assets.Dockerfile using the PascalCase <something>.Dockerfile convention and selects it explicitly with --file
Preserves Razor Class Library (_content) and framework (_framework) asset flow
Uses the base image's established /cdnroot runtime contract
Preserves existing static-asset endpoints after inspecting their role

evals.prompt: Tolk.Web is an ASP.NET Core application that already references Cuemon.AspNetCore.Razor.TagHelpers through Central Package Management, but Directory.Packages.props still pins the package to the obsolete version 6.1.0. It binds AppTagHelperOptions and CdnTagHelperOptions. An earlier migration also created AppAssetOptions: Razor injects AppAssets and calls AppAssets.Value.GetUrl("~/...") for application CSS, JavaScript, fonts, favicon, manifest, and images. Reconcile the application with the current public Cuemon API. Classify reusable Bootstrap, Font Awesome, and htmx package files as shared CDN content. Keep the ordinary Development profile using AppTagHelperOptions.BaseUrlMode = TagHelperBaseUrlMode.Automatic with no App BaseUrl so App assets resolve against the application. Keep Tolk.Web.Assets opt-in, configure its App origin with Automatic mode, a host-only BaseUrl, and ProtocolUriScheme.Http, configure CdnTagHelperOptions in Configured mode when its shared source is available, and configure deployed App/CDN hosts with HTTPS.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the deterministic runner, detects Cuemon from package/project and source evidence, resolves the current latest stable Cuemon.AspNetCore.Razor.TagHelpers version from NuGet.org during plan, and updates the existing PackageVersion while keeping the project PackageReference versionless. It never reuses 6.1.0 or another version from fixtures, examples, templates, or memory, and stops without a package edit if NuGet resolution fails. The runner reports the competing AppAssetOptions/GetUrl abstraction without rewriting it and directs a semantic migration. Application-owned CSS, JavaScript, fonts, favicon, manifest, and images use the actual public app-link, app-script, and app-img custom elements declared by HtmlTargetElement. Shared Bootstrap, Font Awesome, and htmx references use the corresponding cdn-link/cdn-script/cdn-img helpers and remain outside Tolk.Web/wwwroot. Existing rel, type, color, as, and crossorigin attributes are preserved. AppTagHelperOptions and CdnTagHelperOptions remain the only Cuemon asset-location configuration surfaces: ordinary Development uses AppTagHelperOptions.BaseUrlMode = TagHelperBaseUrlMode.Automatic with no App BaseUrl, Tolk.Web.Assets supplies the explicit host-only local App origin with ProtocolUriScheme.Http (and a separate explicitly Configured CDN origin when applicable), and deployment supplies explicit HTTPS hosts. Existing Cuemon ICacheBusting/cache-busting registrations are preserved and consumed by the enhanced Cuemon helpers when the referenced API exposes them; asp-append-version is not blindly copied onto custom elements. AppAssetOptions, its injection, registration, and obsolete configuration are removed only after no consumers remain. The runner remains inspect/plan/verify-only and re-execution is idempotent.
expectations: Runs segregate-assets.cs inspect/plan before making source changes and reports Cuemon and competing-abstraction evidence

evals.prompt: Contoso.Web already has a legacy http-segregated-assets Project launch profile and compose.assets.yml with an app-assets sidecar, but pressing F5 in Visual Studio 2026 starts only the web project and the asset requests fail on localhost:8080. evals.expected_output: The skill explains that commandName Project configures only the application and commandName Docker launches only one project container; neither consumes compose.assets.yml. It keeps the ordinary Contoso.Web Project profile for direct wwwroot development and removes the redundant project-level legacy profile. It adds or reuses an artifact-first production Dockerfile containing only the newest compatible shell-less dhi.io/aspnetcore Alpine runtime and COPY artifacts/publish/ ., plus an artifact-first LocalDevelopment.Dockerfile based on the matching dhi.io/aspnetcore:10-alpine3.23-dev image. It identifies the ASP.NET -dev image as a development-capable runtime rather than an SDK. It defines LocalPublishDirectory in the web csproj, adds a guarded local post-build publish target, and requires CI to publish the same artifact before its production image build. CI also builds or validates Assets.Dockerfile from the same commit. compose.assets.yml directly builds web-app with LocalDevelopment.Dockerfile and the hardened app-assets service with Assets.Dockerfile. The app-assets service sets com.microsoft.visual-studio.project-name to an empty string so Visual Studio does not apply the web project's debugger bootstrap. The profile starts web-app with debugging and app-assets without debugging, launches the web URL, and leaves ordinary Development unchanged. No docker-compose.vs.release.yml is added or retained. The skill does not add DockerfileFile, BuildingInsideVisualStudio, or a custom vsdbg mount. The result is checked with a normal project build that creates the local publish artifact, Docker Compose config, the installed Visual Studio MSBuild, an end-to-end two-container smoke test, and non-root runtime user 65532 when Docker is available. When Visual Studio and Docker are available, completion additionally requires an actual F5 run with Visual Studio in Run mode, /remote_debugger/linux-musl-x64/vsdbg --interpreter=vscode launching the application as its child, no debugger bootstrap in app-assets, and HTTP 200 from both services; a dcproj build or CLI smoke test alone is not IDE proof.

evals.prompt: Segregate the static assets for Fabrikam.WebApp. The solution is Fabrikam.slnx, the web project lives under src/Fabrikam.WebApp, and its ordinary Project launch profile serves https://localhost:51641;http://localhost:51642. I want to keep pressing F5 in Visual Studio.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes Dockerfile, LocalDevelopment.Dockerfile, and Assets.Dockerfile into src/Fabrikam.WebApp beside the .csproj and the wwwroot they relate to, and leaves the repository root free of any Dockerfile. It writes compose.assets.yml, .dockerignore, docker-compose.dcproj, and launchSettings.json at the repository root. Every one of these files is produced from the corresponding literal template under assets/ with placeholders substituted, not reconstructed from memory. Both application Dockerfiles are artifact-first: Dockerfile pins the newest compatible shell-less dhi.io/aspnetcore Alpine runtime and LocalDevelopment.Dockerfile the matching dhi.io/aspnetcore:10-alpine3.23-dev image, each consisting of FROM, WORKDIR, COPY --chown=65532:65532 artifacts/publish/ ., and ENTRYPOINT. Neither declares an SDK stage, runs dotnet restore/build/publish, creates a user with RUN adduser, or uses an mcr.microsoft.com runtime tag. The web project gains LocalPublishDirectory, DockerfileContext, DockerComposeProjectPath, and DockerDefaultTargetOS; a guarded non-CI, non-design-time post-build target publishes into artifacts/publish; artifacts/ is added to .gitignore but deliberately not to .dockerignore. compose.assets.yml declares services web-app and app-assets with different build contexts — repository root with dockerfile src/Fabrikam.WebApp/LocalDevelopment.Dockerfile for the web service, ./src/Fabrikam.WebApp with dockerfile Assets.Dockerfile for the asset service — publishes the web service on the ordinary profile's HTTP port 51642 rather than an invented 5000, publishes the asset origin on 8080, hardens app-assets with read_only, cap_drop ALL, and no-new-privileges, sets com.microsoft.visual-studio.project-name to an empty string on it, omits the obsolete top-level version key, and adds no custom networks block. The root Fabrikam.WebApp.Assets profile uses commandName DockerCompose with composeLaunchUrl http://localhost:51642, starts web-app with debugging and app-assets without debugging, and the ordinary Fabrikam.WebApp Project profile is left untouched. Because the repository CI pipeline has no producer for artifacts/publish, the skill extends .github/workflows/ci-pipeline.yml with a publish job and a docker-build job that builds both Dockerfile and Assets.Dockerfile from the same commit. Cuemon AppTagHelperOptions is bound from SegregatedAssets:App with BaseUrlMode Automatic, an empty BaseUrl, and Scheme Https in appsettings.json, and the Compose environment supplies SegregatedAssets__App__BaseUrl localhost:8080 with Scheme Http. Razor moves to app-link and app-script helpers. verify --run-publish --check-local is run and reports the artifact-first topology as satisfied.
